# Nutrition Plan for High-Performance Rock Climbing

## Daily Calorie & Macro Targets
- **Calories**: ~2,400-2,700/day (depending on training intensity)
- **Protein**: 100-120g/day (1.7-2.1g per kg) for muscle recovery
- **Carbs**: 300-360g/day for sustained energy
- **Fats**: 65-75g/day for hormone health

## Key Food Groups

### Protein Sources (prioritize these)
- Legumes: lentils, chickpeas, black beans, peas
- Dairy: Greek yogurt, cottage cheese, eggs, cheese
- Soy: tofu, tempeh, edamame
- Whole grains: quinoa, buckwheat
- Seeds: sunflower, pumpkin, sesame

### Carbohydrates (sustained energy)
- Oats, brown rice, sweet potatoes, whole grain bread
- Fruits: bananas, dates, berries, apples
- Legumes (dual protein + carb benefit)

### Fats (without nuts)
- Olive oil, avocado, seeds, whole grains
- Dairy products, eggs
- Coconut oil

### Micronutrient Focus
- **Iron**: legumes, leafy greens, fortified cereals
- **Calcium**: dairy, leafy greens, fortified plant milks
- **Magnesium**: seeds, whole grains, dark chocolate
- **Vitamin B12**: fortified plant milks or supplement

## Sample Daily Structure
- **Breakfast**: Oatmeal + Greek yogurt + berries + seeds
- **Mid-morning**: Fruit + seed butter
- **Lunch**: Lentil/chickpea-based grain bowl with veggies
- **Pre-climb snack**: Banana + seed-based energy bar
- **Dinner**: Tofu/tempeh stir-fry with brown rice
- **Evening**: Greek yogurt or cottage cheese

Would you like specific meal ideas or recipes?

# Nutrition Plan for Body Recomposition

## Daily Calorie & Macro Targets

**Calories:** 2,400-2,600/day (modest deficit while training)
- Your BMR is ~1,850 cal; this allows muscle building with slight fat loss

**Macronutrients:**
- **Protein:** 190-210g/day (2.0-2.2g per kg body weight)
- **Fats:** 65-75g/day (25-30% of calories)
- **Carbs:** 270-320g/day (remaining calories)

---

## What to Eat

### Protein Sources (at every meal)
- Chicken breast, turkey, lean ground beef
- Fish (salmon, cod), eggs, Greek yogurt
- Cottage cheese, protein powder, legumes

### Carbohydrates (especially around workouts)
- Oats, brown rice, sweet potatoes, whole grain bread
- Fruit (bananas, berries), pasta
- Time higher carbs around training

### Healthy Fats
- Olive oil, avocado, nuts, seeds
- Fatty fish, nut butters

### Vegetables
- Broccoli, spinach, peppers, carrots (minimal impact on calories, high nutrients)

---

## Practical Tips

✓ Eat in a **slight calorie deficit** (200-300 cal below maintenance)
✓ **Prioritize protein** at every meal
✓ Lift heavy 3-4x/week to preserve muscle
✓ Be patient—body recomposition is slower than pure bulking/cutting
✓ Track intake for 2 weeks to dial in

Would you like specific meal examples?

# Marathon Training Nutrition Plan

## Daily Calorie Target
**2,800-3,200 calories/day** (adjust based on training intensity)

## Macronutrient Distribution

| Nutrient | Amount | Purpose |
|----------|--------|---------|
| **Carbohydrates** | 55-65% (385-520g) | Primary fuel for endurance |
| **Protein** | 15-20% (105-160g) | Muscle repair & recovery |
| **Fat** | 20-25% (62-89g) | Sustained energy & hormone production |

## Sample Daily Structure

### Breakfast
- Oatmeal with banana, berries, honey
- 2 slices whole grain toast with peanut butter
- Greek yogurt

### Mid-Morning Snack
- Energy bar or rice cakes with jam
- Sports drink (if training)

### Lunch
- Grilled chicken or fish
- Brown rice or pasta
- Vegetables (broccoli, sweet potato)

### Pre-Workout (1-3 hours before)
- Banana + energy drink, or toast with jam

### Post-Workout (within 30-60 min)
- Chocolate milk, protein smoothie, or bagel with turkey

### Dinner
- Lean meat/fish
- Whole grain/rice
- Vegetables + olive oil

### Evening Snack (if needed)
- Fruit, whole grain crackers, or low-fat dairy

## Hydration
- **Daily**: 3-4 liters water
- **During training**: Sports drinks for efforts >90 minutes

## Carb-Loading (3 days before race)
Increase carbs to **70% of calories** while reducing fiber and fat slightly.
